accuracy.reason: All five objectives correctly define interaction roles, shared HTTP/application semantics, local-session dependence versus stateless handlers, finite shared-service resources and uncertain missing responses. No false capacity or no-state claim.

evidence.quote: Stateless does not mean no persistent data, authentication or state anywhere in the system.

mechanisms.reason: Connects request fields to interpretation/checks/work/response and state placement to replacement/failure. Separates reported error from a lost response after possible effect. LessonDiagram matches exchanges, example local sessions and client/server costs.

evidence.quote: processing may have succeeded and only the response was lost.

coherence.reason: Only program memory and network delivery prerequisites are needed. Roles lead to protocol, retained context, service tradeoffs and an integrated interaction explanation; each card supplies its objective.

evidence.quote: Locate persistent application data and any session context separately.

decisions.reason: Balances centralized shared behavior against round trips, overload/rejection and dependency failure. Client-local/offline benefits carry synchronization costs; protected access remains server-enforced and retry decisions depend on outcome uncertainty.

evidence.quote: the client/server model alone guarantees neither capacity nor availability.

clarity.reason: Defines protocol, API and session state when first used, avoids hardware-role confusion, and gives short concrete server-A examples. The generic request trace is sufficient without a mandatory recurring story. Diagram/shared assets inspected only.

evidence.quote: These are roles in an interaction, not types of computer.

outcomes.reason: Defines client initiation and server handling independently of browser/hardware/location, including dual-role service calls. Traces method/URL/headers/body and status/content while distinguishing protocol syntax from application meaning and operational success.

Explains session context, local-memory dependence and rerouting/loss, request/shared-store context for replaceable handlers and remaining storage dependency. Connects central shared rules to network waits, unavailable dependencies and finite overload without automatic scale/availability.

Gives a coherent generic shared-data operation, locates persistent data and session context separately, supplies HTTP contents and access/work/outcome steps, and distinguishes explicit reported failure from unknown processing/delivery outcome. No response is correctly not evidence of no effect.

sourceChecks.claim: RFC 9110 section 3.3 defines request-sending client and responding server as programs/interaction roles; a program can act in both roles. No browser or machine-class restriction is asserted.

RFC 9110 describes method/target/header/content and response status semantics, including errors; application payload conventions remain separate. OWASP REST guidance checked in this review supports service-side access checks rather than hidden controls.

Azure autoscaling explicitly advises avoiding instance dependence and assumptions about subsequent routing. Externalized/request-carried context explains why equivalent handlers can replace one another while shared storage remains a dependency.

MDN distinguishes client/server purposes, shared dynamic data, centralized access and optional server computation; finite resources and failed remote dependencies are correctly presented as costs, not unlimited model guarantees.

RFC 9110 section 9.2.2 explains retries after communications fail before a response is readable, distinguishing idempotent from unsafe automatic retries. This supports unknown outcome rather than assuming processing never happened.
